findings.title: `--estimate` reports BUY and prints a ceiling command for a refusal that may not be about ceilings
findings.description: With `check_ceilings=False`, `judge_estimate` returns `Estimate.BUY` as soon as the verdict is not `nothing_to_buy`. That skips the `summary["verdict"] != VERDICT_ALLOWED` check, along with the ceiling checks (lines 242-245). `_estimate_only` (`scripts/cutover_304_first_purchase.py:273-275`) then prints `the PM runs: sudo ... --per-pass N --cap-30d M` whenever the outcome is BUY. Only the ceiling-based refusals are meant to be skipped. Any other refusal reason in `summary["reasons"]` is reported as BUY, with a ceiling command that will not clear it. The operator would run the root command and only learn of the real refusal on the real run. The docstring says only "short or unset ceilings are not a stop". The code skips the whole verdict check instead. The test `test_estimate_prints_the_command_and_buys_nothing` uses `reasons: ["ceiling"]`, so it never exercises a non-ceiling refusal. Fix: in estimate mode, still stop on a refused verdict whose reasons are not ceiling-only, or print `summary["reasons"]` alongside the command. Add a test for a non-ceiling refusal.

findings.title: Resubmit time comparison has no timezone guard, unlike the dataset-edge parser
findings.description: `resubmit_origins` parses `requested_at` with `datetime.fromisoformat` and only checks that it parses. `_check_resubmit` then compares it with `since`, which is tz-aware (`datetime.now(UTC).isoformat`). If a row ever renders a naive timestamp, `made < since` raises `TypeError`. `main` catches only `KeyError` and `ValueError` (`scripts/cutover_304_first_purchase.py:246-252`), so this becomes an unrecorded traceback after the install step, not a narrated `FAILED:` stop. `purchase_verdicts._edge_of` already guards this case (`edge.tzinfo is None`). The two parsers handle timestamps inconsistently. Fix: reject a naive `requested_at` in `resubmit_origins` with a `CutoverError`, as `_edge_of` does. Add a test for it.

findings.title: The "no end date" rule over `TICK_UNIVERSE` history is implemented twice
findings.description: `coverage_reads()` in `cutover_304_evidence.py` and `latest_want_end()` in `scripts/purchase_verdicts.py:61-74` each walk `TICK_UNIVERSE[*].history`. Each raises its own `"{product} {schema} want has no end date"` error. This is the "one value, one source" and DRY situation the project rules warn about. If the open-end policy changes, two places must change. Fix: expose one iterator or helper that yields the bounded wants and raises on an open end, and build both functions on it.

findings.title: `cutover_304_*` names now carry every purchase slice
findings.description: The module docstring now says the script is "shared by every purchase slice". The file names, the argparse `prog="cutover_304_first_purchase.py"`, and the `cutover_304_checks` and `cutover_304_evidence` imports still say 304. The new modules (`purchase_accounting`, `purchase_verdicts`) use the neutral naming. The mixed naming is workable and is explained in the docstring. A later rename to `purchase_cutover_*` would remove the drift.

findings.title: Test typing is loose in places and several test files are large
findings.description:
These items are minor. The project guidance calls for typed signatures, with mypy on touched files.
- `_status(...) -> object` is passed to `check_dataset_edge`, which expects `subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]`. A type checker would reject this. The return type should be `subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]`.
- `_request(...) -> dict` and `units: list[dict] | None` use bare generics.
- `_parser()` calls `__doc__.split(...)`, and `__doc__` is `str | None`. A strict checker flags this (`scripts/cutover_304_first_purchase.py:209`).
- `test_cutover_304_first_purchase.py` is now about 770 lines and `test_purchase_verdicts.py` about 365, against the ~300-line guidance. Splitting the 307 evidence and gate tests into their own files would match how the production code was split.

findings.title: Verified: request symbols, calendar lookup, and exception handling
findings.description:
I read the underlying code for these claims.
- `tick_debug_cmds._cell` renders list values as a comma-joined string, so `product_of_symbols` parses the shape the CLI actually emits. `test_bar_job_dirs_read_the_rows_the_real_cli_renders` runs the real `_cell`, so the fixture matches production.
- `calendar_for_product` raises `KeyError` for an unknown product, and `calendar_for` converts that to a `CutoverError` with no default calendar. This replaces the old hard-coded `CME_EQUITY` fallback and fixes GC bars being checked against the equity calendar.
- Exception handling follows the project rules. Each catch is specific and chained with `from exc`. `main`'s `SystemExit` catch is a documented process-boundary handler.
- Unknown session buckets, missing accounting keys, and a baseline that predates 307 all fail loudly (`purchase_verdicts._unaccounted`, `purchase_accounting`, `_baseline_records`) instead of defaulting.
- The gate-issue and dataset-edge checks run before any state write or install, and tests assert that nothing is written on refusal.

structured_findings.summary: `--estimate` reports BUY and prints a ceiling command for a refusal that may not be about ceilings
Resubmit time comparison has no timezone guard, unlike the dataset-edge parser
The "no end date" rule over `TICK_UNIVERSE` history is implemented twice
`cutover_304_*` names now carry every purchase slice
Test typing is loose in places and several test files are large
